device_template.name: Fronius installation (Solar API site totals)
device_template.description:
The whole INSTALLATION in one call — GetPowerFlowRealtimeData.fcgi — not a device on a bus.

Measured on a production DataManager 2026-09-13: 89 ms per call, and the values behind it refresh every 2.5-3.3 s. Polling faster than about 2 s returns the same number twice; the datalogger polls its own RS-485 side on its own rhythm and we cannot outrun it.

What makes this worth a source of its own: house load, autonomy and self-consumption are NOT derivable from the inverters. Nothing in an inverter's register map knows what the house consumed. Sum the inverters and you get generation; you still cannot say how much of it stayed on site.

Grid and battery power ship UNTICKED. A meter wired at the grid connection reports the same flow first-hand and faster (measured: 1.1 s against 2.5 s here), so taking it from the site view would be a slower second copy. Tick them only when there is no such meter.

Sign convention follows the source: grid negative while exporting, battery negative while charging. Flipping it would make our number disagree with the inverter's own display.

The URL carries no ${unit_id}: an installation is one thing, so this group holds exactly one unit.

realtime.description: power flow and ratios (source refreshes ~2.5 s)

registers.name: power_pv
registers.label: PV generation
registers.description: The number the whole installation is judged by, and the DataManager computes it itself.

registers.name: power_load
registers.label: House load
registers.description: Not derivable from the inverters: nothing in their register maps knows what the house drew.

registers.name: power_grid
registers.label: Grid power
registers.description: OFF by default: a meter wired on the grid connection reports this faster and first-hand. Tick it only when there is no such meter.

registers.name: power_battery
registers.label: Battery power
registers.description: OFF by default: null on an installation without storage, and a battery reports itself better.

registers.name: autonomy
registers.label: Autonomy
registers.description: Computed on the datalogger from generation and load together; we cannot derive it from either alone.

registers.name: self_consumption
registers.label: Self-consumption
registers.description: Same: a site-level ratio, not a device reading.

registers.name: energy_today
registers.label: Energy today
registers.description: Site.E_Day is the sum over the inverters still answering: it drops at sunset as they sleep, so the gateway holds the day\u2019s maximum and adopts only the midnight reset (daily: true).

registers.name: energy_year
registers.label: Energy this year
registers.description: OFF by default: a slow counter most installations read from the daily total instead.
